text_simplified: This text discusses the rights of children upon their parents, mentioning several Prophetic hadiths that urge the sound tarbiyah (upbringing) of children and teaching them prayer and charity. It also highlights the importance of treating children with rifq (gentleness) and kindness, avoiding physical or psychological harm. The goal is to raise parents' awareness of their responsibilities toward their children.

review_defects.why: The Arabic 'صالحة' means righteous/pious, not merely 'sound'; the translation loses the religious and moral connotation.
The Arabic 'اللين' means gentleness/leniency, not 'kindness'; the translation substitutes a different virtue and also inconsistently transliterates only one of the two terms.
The title transliterates 'Tarbiyah' without translation, while the body translates it as 'upbringing'; for consistency and clarity, the title should use 'upbringing' or include a gloss.
